clue.text: Fair-minded article calling for exactly what's needed

parts.note: a fair-minded person is just, impartial
the definite article is the word the
a calling or occupation is a job

explanation.surface: Someone even-handed writes a piece urging that the right thing be done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a newspaper piece but supplies the grammatical article; 'calling' is a vocation, not a demand.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something perfectly suited to the purpose, the ideal thing.

clue.text: I hear you have changed in China's revolution

indicators.note: the setter says he hears the word, so the letter that sounds like it is used

parts.note: the word you is said aloud as the letter U

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the friend

parts.note: china is rhyming slang (china plate = mate) for a friend, a pal

indicators.note: changed tells us to rearrange the letters of the word have

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a person has altered during China's political revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' turns HAVE into HEAV. China plate is Cockney rhyming slang for mate; the 's reads as 'is', joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent upheaval is a sudden overturning, a synonym for a revolution in society.

clue.text: Bug found in milk

definitions.meaning: to bug a phone is to fit a listening device to it
to milk a resource is to draw from it, exploit it

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a wiretap bugs a line, and to drain or exploit something is to draw on it.

clue.text: Over time judge shows compassion

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed over another comes before it

parts.note: to hear a case is to judge it in court

explanation.surface: As the years pass, a judge shows mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart is a common figurative word for warmth and sympathy toward others.

clue.text: Evergreen salesman — one journalists upset

indicators.note: in a down answer upset turns the whole run of pieces upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a sales representative is a rep
I is the Roman numeral for one
the NUJ is the UK's National Union of Journalists

explanation.surface: A salesman and a group of reporters are dismayed by something everlasting.
explanation.definitionFit: The juniper is a coniferous shrub that keeps its needles all year round.

clue.text: Article packed by men and boys at sea? Certainly not

indicators.note: packed by means the article is wrapped inside the jumbled letters
at sea means confused, so the letters of men and boys are jumbled

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Asks whether a newspaper piece was written by men and boys on a ship, and answers no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges the seven letters into BYNOMES; 'packed by' puts the article inside. The question mark admits the surface is fanciful.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm idiom of refusal or denial, meaning not at all.

clue.text: Cope with celebrity

definitions.meaning: to ... a problem is to confront and deal with it
a famous person is a well-known ...

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: confronting a difficulty, and a familiar public figure seen on screens.

clue.text: I've sheep and pig food in fine cupboard

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: in puts the pig food inside the cupboard

parts.note: a locker is a small lockable cupboard
mast is the fallen nuts of beech and oak, fed to pigs

explanation.surface: A farmer declares ownership of sheep and keeps pig feed in a good cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep owner or breeder can say this; the definition speaks in the first person of someone keeping a flock.

clue.text: Customer with one pound in small change

indicators.note: in puts the pound and one inside the coin

parts.note: a cent is a coin of small value
L (from Latin libra) stands for a pound
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A shopper hands over a pound and gets a few coppers back.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is a person who buys goods or services, a patron.

clue.text: Minister having mountain retreat in the distance

indicators.note: in places the turned-back mountain inside the measure

parts.note: a chain is an old unit of distance, 22 yards

indicators.note: to retreat is to go back, so the mountain is read backwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain

explanation.surface: A clergyman owns a mountain hideaway far off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreat' looks like a noun for the hideaway but is the reversal signal; a chain is a surveyor's length of 22 yards, used for cricket pitches.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaplain is a clergyman attached to an institution, a minister of religion.

clue.text: Sex: that's on the retreat

indicators.note: on means the abbreviation is placed after the retreat in the across answer

parts.note: a nook is a secluded corner, a retreat
ie (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: A remark that lovemaking happens on a getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful slang term for sexual activity, chiefly British.

clue.text: Tick off favourite on short race meeting programme

indicators.note: on means the favourite follows the cut programme in the across answer
short means the last letter is cut from the programme

parts.note: a race card lists the runners at a meeting
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Mark off the favourite on a brief race card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick off' suggests marking a list but means scold; 'favourite' suggests a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for reprimanding them, calling them on the carpet.

clue.text: Master set theory

parts.note: a pro, a professional, is a master of a skill
to set something is to position it

explanation.surface: Grasp mathematical set theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master set theory' reads as an instruction to learn maths; 'set' is the verb, not the mathematical noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition is a statement put forward for discussion, an idea or hypothesis.

clue.text: Squash — sort not finished during quizzes

indicators.note: during puts the shortened kind inside the quizzes

parts.note: to pump someone is to quiz them for information

indicators.note: not finished drops the last letter

parts.note: a sort is a kind

explanation.surface: A game of squash played during question sessions, with one type left incomplete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squash' looks like the racket game but is the vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumpkins belong to the squash family of gourds.

clue.text: Play in pubs, not clubs, in holiday island

indicators.note: pubs, not clubs means the bars replace the clubs letter

parts.note: Majorca is a Spanish island popular with British holidaymakers
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
two pubs are two bars

explanation.surface: A theatre show staged in bars rather than nightclubs on a sunny island.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the C of MAJORCA for BAR BAR. This is a play by George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1905 drama by George Bernard Shaw about a Salvation Army officer.

clue.text: Stroke of luck with this sort of clue analysis

parts.note: a lucky break is a stroke of luck
the clue sits in the down column of the grid

explanation.surface: A fortunate chance helps the solver with a tricky clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A breakdown is a detailed analysis of figures into parts.

clue.text: I wasn't mad about poem by Anglo-Irish satirist

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters wrap round the poem
mad means the letters of the phrase are wildly rearranged

parts.note: If is a famous poem by Kipling

explanation.surface: A protest from a writer insisting he was sane about a poem by an Irish satirist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' shuffles I WASNT into SWTIAN, which goes round IF. Jonathan Swift was rumoured to have gone mad late in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Swiftian describes writing in the manner of Jonathan Swift, the Dublin-born satirist.

clue.text: Poor place the owner soon abandoned

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild, unrestrained, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: A rundown property that its proprietor quickly left.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a small, dull, backward settlement with little to offer.

clue.text: Exceptional leader of troops recruiting soldiers for scrap

indicators.note: recruiting means taking the soldiers in among the other letters

parts.note: odd means unusual, exceptional

indicators.note: leader of means the first letter of the word

parts.note: men are soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: An outstanding commander enlists troops for a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrap' looks like a fight but means a leftover piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddment is a leftover fragment, a remnant or scrap.

clue.text: Say, crew cut and run fast reportedly on occasion

indicators.note: on means the first piece sits above the second in a down answer
reportedly means the word sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: to hare is to run very fast
a do is a party, an occasion

explanation.surface: A sailor's team cuts short and dashes off at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crew cut' reads as a ship's crew being reduced; it is a short haircut, with 'Say' marking it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is one example of a hairstyle.

clue.text: Scared to score drug in flat

indicators.note: in puts the score and drug inside the flat

parts.note: a pad is slang for a flat or apartment
to nick is to make a notch, score
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone afraid of buying drugs in an apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'score drug' suggests buying narcotics; here 'score' means notch.
explanation.definitionFit: To have panicked is to have been seized by fear, frightened.

clue.text: Disoriented after commercial break st break

indicators.note: after places the break behind the commercial

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: Someone confused after an ad break.
explanation.definitionFit: Adrift means lost or without bearings, figuratively off course.

clue.text: Comrade of old-soldier and old lady turned up

indicators.note: in a down answer turned up means the whole string reads from the bottom

parts.note: O is short for old and GI is an American soldier
ma is a mother, an old lady

explanation.surface: A friend of a veteran and his mother arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, a companion or comrade.

clue.text: Duke: right, wrong, in glasses? 9

indicators.note: in puts the right and wrong inside the glasses

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of spectacles
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A nobleman wonders whether right and wrong appear through his spectacles.
explanation.walkthrough: The Duke is from Shakespeare's Twelfth Night; the 9 cross-reference is a stray in this copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Orsino is the Duke of Illyria in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.

clue.text: Prevailing sea current written about in The Odyssey, say

indicators.note: in places the turned piece inside the long poem

parts.note: Homer's Odyssey is an example of an epic

indicators.note: written about means the letters are set down turned round

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A dominant ocean flow described in Homer's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written about' turns the sea and current round into IDEM, which sits inside the poem; I is the symbol physicists use for current.
explanation.definitionFit: Epidemic as an adjective means widespread, rife.

clue.text: Sound of alarm from beekeeper, either way

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A beekeeper's startled cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'either way': the letters lie in 'beekeeper' read forwards (bEEKeeper) and backwards (beeKEEper turned round).
explanation.definitionFit: Eek is an exclamation of fright or alarm.

clue.text: Dress suit taken from warehouse, out east

indicators.note: taken from means the suit letters are removed

parts.note: a godown is a warehouse in India and East Asia
to do is to suit, as in that will do

explanation.surface: A suit removed from a storehouse in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' and 'suit' are both garments in the surface; 'suit' is the verb meaning serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A gown is a long formal dress.

clue.text: Way of making contacts one wants to get a number back in business

definitions.text: Way of making contacts one wants to get

indicators.note: back means the number is read in reverse

parts.note: ten is a number
a firm that is working is in business

explanation.surface: Someone eager to have a figure returned at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Building a web of business contacts by mixing socially, a deliberate career practice.
